newsitem.title: USA: U.S. jobless claims fell in latest week.
newsitem.headline: U.S. jobless claims fell in latest week.

text.p: U.S. Labor Department report of initial state jobless benefit claims, seasonally adjusted.
Week Ended Initial Claims 4-Week Avg. Continued Claims
R-Revised, Nov 30 Initial Claims from 336,000 and Nov 23 from 344,000; Nov 30 Four-Week Average from 337,750 and Nov 23 from 336,750; Nov 23 Continued Claims from 2,467,000 and Nov 16 from 2,401,000.
Wall Street economists had forecast initial jobless claims of 341,000 in the December 7 week.
The department said claims in the December 7 week were at their lowest point since claims of 317,000 were reported in the week ended August 31, 1996.
The department said 15 states reported decreases in claims exceeding 1,000 on an unadjusted basis in the week ended November 30, the latest period for which data are available.
Among the largest were California, with 34,860 fewer initial claims, North Carolina with 5,684 fewer, Pennsylvania with 3,822, New Jersey with 3,780 and Florida with 3,285.

California and New Jersey said the shorter workweek due to the Thanksgiving Day holiday was the reason for the decrease in claims. Meanwhile, North Carolina and Pennsylvania said they saw fewer layoffs in textiles and transportation equipment. Pennsylvania also said there were fewer layoffs in food, primary metals and agriculture.
In Florida, fewer layoffs were reported in construction, trade, services, manufacturing and agriculture.
Labor said four states reported increases in initial claims exceeding 1,000, unadjusted, in the December 7 week.
They were Wisconsin, with 10,192 additional claims filings, Indiana with 1,987, Arkansas with 1,685 and Massachusetts with 1,550.
Wisconsin reported layoffs in construction, trade and manufacturing, while Indiana saw layoffs in food, apparel, furniture, lumber, primary metals and transportation equipment.
Arkansas had layoffs in the electrical equipment industry, and Massachusetts did not cite a reason.
